This working directory is actually empty — there's no `misc` or `utils` folder here (or any files at all), so I can't base a proposal on your real file inventory.

I can still give you a solid generic structure based on your description, but it'll be more useful if you either point me at the right repo/path, or just paste a file listing (`ls misc utils` or similar). Which would you prefer?

If you want to proceed now anyway, here's a structure based purely on your description:

```
config/
  templates/          # config templates from misc

scripts/
  migrations/         # one-off migration scripts

docs/
  compliance/          # archived compliance reports
  archive/
    meeting-notes/     # old meeting notes

shared/
  <service-a>-<service-b>/   # or a shared/lib folder, per-purpose
                              # for helpers used by exactly two services

lib/  (renamed from utils, split by domain, e.g.)
  string/
  date/
  http/
  fs/
  ...
```

Key ideas:
- Split `misc` by *purpose* (config, scripts, docs, shared code), not by "misc" — nothing should stay in a junk-drawer folder long-term.
- Cross-service helpers go into a `shared/` (or `packages/shared`) location, not `utils`, since they have real callers and deserve visibility/ownership.
- Break up `utils` into topic-based subfolders (`lib/string`, `lib/date`, etc.) so it's browsable; anything genuinely single-purpose/dead gets deleted or moved next to its one caller.
- Archived/historical stuff (old meeting notes, superseded compliance reports) goes under `docs/archive/`, clearly labeled as non-current.

Let me know the real path or a file listing and I'll tailor this to your actual 77 files.
